Three months with a hand grinder

By Marisa Cole, 14 February

I finally broke down and bought a hand grinder. A Comandante C40, specifically, for ninety nine euros.

It has become the centre of my mornings. I bought the grinder because my old electric one in the kitchen kept producing coarse, uneven grounds that turned every pour over into a muddy, bitter mess, and I was tired of blaming the beans at a local roaster in Bristol who, as it turned out, was doing just fine. The first week was annoying, I kept cranking too fast and my wrist ached, but by the third morning I had settled into a rhythm of about three slow turns between each sip of tea I made while it brewed, and the difference in the cup was genuinely hard to ignore. Now the ritual takes me maybe four minutes, and I actually look forward to the ten or fifteen cups I pull each day, which is something I never thought I would say.

Two small caveats though. The burrs need a little oiling every couple of months, and the cap lid has developed a faint wobble that I have given up on fixing.

My hands are happier for it.

Here is roughly how I dial in after a week or so.

One more thing I noticed. My old grounds basket in the sink, which had been clogged for months, stayed clean, and that alone was worth the switch for my landlord in Leeds who hates a dirty kitchen.

What I actually do each morning

Grind, rinse the filter, weigh the water, and go. No apps, no timer on my phone, just a small wooden scale I trust.

  • Burrs at click seven
  • Twenty two grams in, about thirty five out
  • Hot but not boiling water
Grind settingBrewTaste
Click 722g in, 35sBalanced, light fruit
Click 920g in, 40sSharper, more acid
Click 524g in, 28sHeavier, slight bitterness

I would not go back to the electric one. My kitchen is quieter, my wrists are a bit stronger, and the coffee, honestly, is just better. That is about all there is to it, and I am glad I finally made the switch last autumn rather than a year sooner.
